title: Give a key an expiry
summary: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit.
introduction: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit. Your task: Wait briefly and compare the remaining time.
learningObjectives: Wait briefly and compare the remaining time.
Explain the example for give a key an expiry

blocks.text: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit. It is useful for temporary data such as a short-lived cached answer.
Use a local Redis server and redis-cli. Commands here use cma: practice keys only. Redis commands do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Do not connect these exercises to a production database.

blocks.code:
SET cma:tip "Water the plants" EX 30
TTL cma:tip
blocks.title: Give a key an expiry

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `TTL` reports remaining life in seconds. Its result changes as time passes and uses special values for missing or non-expiring keys.

blocks.text: TTL reports the remaining life in seconds, near 30 if checked immediately.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: TTL changes with time. A missing key returns -2, so do not expect one fixed number after waiting.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Wait briefly and compare the remaining time.
